paper.title: Combinatorial Bandits without Total Order for Arms

settings.name_in_paper: Combinatorial bandits with set-dependent binary rewards under weak optimal set consistency (no total order)
unmapped: Reward distribution of each base arm depends on the selected set s (P(a|s)); set reward is the sum of base-arm rewards
Weak optimal set consistency: for any suboptimal set s and arm a in s and s*, P(a|s) >= P(a|s*); no total order on arms assumed
settings.definition_quote: At each time step $t$, the online learner selects a $s(t) \in \Scal$ ($|s(t)| = k$ by definition). The online player then observes the stochastic reward $X_{i, s(t)}$ of all the arms in $s(t)$. ... Here we focus on the binary reward with $X_{i, s} \in \cbr{0, 1}$ ... For any sub-optimal set $s$ and any $a$ that is common in $s, s^*$, we assume $P(a|s) \ge P(a|s^*)$.

settings.name_in_paper: Combinatorial bandits with bounded set-dependent rewards in [0,B] under extended weak optimal set consistency
unmapped: Reward distribution of each base arm depends on the selected set s
Extended weak optimal set consistency: E[X_{i,s}] >= E[X_{i,s*}] for arms common to suboptimal s and s*; no total order
settings.definition_quote: For any set $s$, the reward $X_{i, s}$s are now generated from any bounded distribution with $ {X_{i, s}} \in [0, B]$, and the online learner observes all rewards $X_{i, s}$.

source.label: thm:instance_dependent_upper_bound
source.quote: For combinatorial bandits problem under \Cref{assumption:weak}, run \Cref{alg:UCB} with parameter $\alpha \ge 2$, we have R(T) \le \frac{8 \alpha k^{\frac{3}{2}} n \log T}{\epsilon} + \frac{30 \alpha k^{2} n \log T}{\epsilon} + n = O\rbr{\frac{\alpha k^{2} n \log T}{\epsilon}}.

results.notes: Paper's n (number of arms) mapped to d, set size k to m. Regret defined as E[Q(s*) - Q(s(t))] = pseudo-regret. Proof uses ln T >= 5.

bound.expression_latex: 2\sqrt{\alpha kn T \log T} + 15k^2\sqrt{\alpha n T \log T}

source.label: thm:instance_independent_upper_bound
source.quote: For combinatorial bandits problem under \Cref{assumption:weak}, run \Cref{alg:UCB} with parameter $\alpha \ge 2$, we have R(T) \le 2\sqrt{\alpha kn T \log T} + 15k^2\sqrt{\alpha n T \log T}= O\rbr{k^{2}\sqrt{\alpha n T \log T}}.

conditions: reward model M1: at most one arm in the selected set has non-zero reward (mutually exclusive rewards, e.g. MNL/RUM)
instance satisfies weak optimal set consistency
for any online learning algorithm (proof treats algorithms with o(T^a) regret for all a>0 and argues others trivially)

source.label: thm:regret_lower_bound
source.quote: For any online learning algorithm, there exists an environment instance with reward model $\Mcal1$ and satisfies \Cref{assumption:weak}, such that the algorithm induces a regret of $R(T) = \Omega\rbr{\frac{n \log T}{k\epsilon}}$.

results.notes: Construction uses n+k-1 arms; arms have total order in the hard instance. Proof is via consistent-algorithm argument.

source.label: thm:regret_lower_bound
source.quote: There exists another environment instance with reward model $\Mcal2$ and satisfies \Cref{assumption:weak}, such that the algorithm induces a regret of $R(T) = \Omega\rbr{\frac{n \log T}{\epsilon}}$.

results.notes: Hard instance uses success probabilities 1/2 and 1/2-eps.

source.label: coro:extension
source.quote: For combinatorial bandits problem with feedback model under \Cref{assumption:extended}, run the modified \Cref{alg:UCB} with parameter $\alpha \ge 2$, we have R(T) = O\rbr{\min\rbr{\frac{\alpha k^{2}B^{2} n \log T}{\epsilon}, k^{2}B\sqrt{\alpha n T \log T}}}

results.notes: Combined min of gap-dependent and gap-independent bounds as stated; rewards rescaled [0,B] mapped to bounded_01.
